author: Rahul kp
title: Decode Coding
simple_words: Each letter is changed by one fixed rule. Find the rule from one pair, then test it on the next letter.

definitions.meaning: A word is changed into a code by a hidden rule. You find the rule and apply it to a new word.
A=1, B=2 ... Z=26. Shifts and mirror pairs are easy when you work with these numbers.

key_points: Write the ==position numbers== of the word letter by letter, and the code letters below them.
Compare each pair: is the gap the same (+n or −n), or does it change?
Check the rule on ==every letter==, not only the first one.
!!Test the rule on all letters!! before you mark the option; many wrong options fit only the first letter.

rows: Gap is equal in all pairs
Code is the same word backwards

insight.punchline: One pair shows it, all pairs prove it!
insight.text: The rule is the same for every letter of the word, so one wrong letter means you have the wrong rule.

memory_trick.explanation: A and Z, B and Y are mirror twins and their places always add to 27. EJOTY gives the places 5, 10, 15, 20, 25 as anchors for counting.

steps: Write place numbers of the word
Write place numbers of the code
Find the gap for each letter
Name the type and test all letters
Apply the rule to the new word
exam_tip: Wrap-around: after Z comes A again. When a shift goes past Z, subtract 26 from the place number.

doubt.question: Forward shift or backward shift: how do I know?
doubt.answer: Compare the code place with the word place. If the code is bigger it is +n; if smaller it is −n. Add 26 if the value goes below 1.

mistakes_hook: one slip and the code breaks

mistakes.wrong: Checking only the first letter and picking the option
mistakes.right: Test the rule on every letter of the word before choosing the option.

mistakes.wrong: Using the mirror rule as place + code = 26
mistakes.right: For opposite letters the sum of places is 27 (A=1 and Z=26).

mistakes.wrong: Stopping at Z when a forward shift goes beyond it
mistakes.right: Wrap around: after Z the count continues from A, so subtract 26.

mistakes.wrong: Applying a fixed shift when the gaps change along the word
mistakes.right: If the gaps differ, look for a pattern such as +1, +2, +3 and apply it to the new word.

check_notes: Checker 1: Key points 3 and 4 say the same thing (both tell you to test the rule on every letter). Suggested fix: change key point 4 to something new, e.g. 'Note whether the code is a forward shift, a backward shift or a mirror before you apply it to the new word.'

Checker 1: The doubt answer can confuse a student when the shift wraps past Z. It says a bigger code place means +n and a smaller one means -n, but Y->B (25->2) is a forward shift of +3 with wrap-around, which that rule would read as -23. Suggested fix: 'Compare the code place with the word place. If the code is bigger it is +n; if smaller it is -n. Add 26 if the value goes below 1. If a big gap like -23 shows up, read it as the short forward wrap (+3) and check which reading fits all the letters.'

Checker 2: Key point 3 and key point 4 say the same thing (test the rule on every letter). This is wording polish only. Merge them or replace one with a new point, for example 'also check for a reversed word or a changing shift'. All facts are correct: A=1 to Z=26, EJOTY = 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, mirror sum 27, wrap-around by ±26.
